chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ) وَمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ عُمَرَ. ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا، غَالِي الْمَذْهَبِ.

translations.en: He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar. Very weak, a ghālī in madhhab.

en.summary: Miyyāh al-Madāʾinī is characterized in al-Ghadāʾirī’s *Kitab al-Duʿafāʾ* as a 'very weak' narrator who transmitted from Imam al-Sādiq (AS) and Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, reflecting the critical scrutiny applied to early transmitters. His designation as 'ghālī' (exaggerator) highlights the theological tensions of the era, where certain narrators were deemed unreliable due to their tendency toward extreme views or innovations (ghuluww) that diverged from mainstream Shia orthodoxy.
en.seo_question: Who is Miyyah al-Madaini and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.مِيَّاحٌ: Miyyah, a proper name of a narrator.
key_terms.الْمَدَائِنِيُّ: Al-Madāʾinī, a nisba indicating origin from al-Madāʾin (Ctesiphon).
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا: Very weak, a technical term in jarh wa ta'dil (criticism and praise) indicating low reliability.
key_terms.غَالِي الْمَذْهَبِ: Ghālī in madhhab, meaning an exaggerator in theological beliefs, often associated with the Ghulat sect.
